title: microrelease-triggering-patterns-and-sweeps-wip
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a lightweight, cross-functional pattern for 'microreleases' — very small exposure increases with automated observational sweeps — intended to be a lower-friction alternative to full multi-cohort canaries for low-risk changes (prompt tweaks, small prompt template rollouts, UI copy with LLM outputs). It focuses on triggers, monitoring sweep design, stakeholder comms, and simple rollback heuristics.

Why microreleases?
- Lower cognitive overhead than a full A/B experiment for trivial changes.
- Faster signal: quick observational sweeps let us detect regressions on important slices without full metric instrumentation.
- Good for iterative prompt tuning and rapid fixes where the blast radius is small.

Pattern overview (high-level):
1) Define scope & owner: single primary owner + 1 reviewer from SRE or Observability.
2) Safety gates: a short checklist (see "Preflight checklist") that must be green.
3) Release window & traffic pattern: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% over discrete time windows OR event-triggered jumps if signals remain green.
4) Sweep cadence: automated sweep after each exposure increase (5–15 min). Human review at the 2% step.
5) Rollback trigger: any critical SLA regression, quality gating failure, or user-facing error spike.

Preflight checklist (quick):
- Owner assigned and Slack channel created (#microrelease-<shortname>)
- Change description + hypothesis stated in release note (one-paragraph)
- Key metrics (latency p95, error rate, core quality metric for prompt) defined with thresholds
- A lightweight canary config (traffic slices) baked into the rollout plan
- Smoke test script ready (curl + auth token) and passes locally
- Fallback model/version available and smoke-tested

Trigger patterns (examples):
- Time-based: advance at fixed intervals if all sweep probes are green (0.5% for 15m, 2% for 30m, etc.)
- Signal-based: advance when the last N sweeps show metric drift < threshold (e.g., p95 latency +1% and QA metric delta < 0.5%)
- Manual gate: stay at the 2% slice until Product/PM signs off (used for UX-visible changes)

Observational sweep design (what to test every step):
- Latency and error probes: p50/p95/p99, 5xx/4xx rates, percent timeout
- Quality probes: a small, curated prompt set (20–50 prompts) that represents critical user journeys; measure BLEU/ROUGE-like scoring where applicable or regenerate/compare to golden outputs using heuristics
- Safety probes: token-level safety checks + model toxicity signals for public-facing features
- Real-user sampling: sample N real requests (100–500) and run a fast heuristic classification for obvious regressions (N depends on traffic)

Sweep automation checklist:
- Run sweep every 5–15 minutes after an exposure bump (cron job or built-in rollout hook)
- Generate a short summary with pass/fail tiles and links to dashboards
- Post summary to Slack channel with clear thumbs-up/thumbs-down reactions for quick human acknowledgment

Communication templates (short):
- Initial post (owner): "Starting microrelease <shortname>. Hypothesis: <one line>. Traffic: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5%. Key metrics: latency p95 (<300ms), error rate (<0.2%), QA metric delta (<1%). Monitoring: <dashboard link>. @oncall please watch."
- Sweep result (automated): "Sweep @ 10:14 UTC — 0.5% slice — latency p95 +0.3% (OK), errors +0.05% (OK), QA metric -0.6% (ALERT). Owner: please review. [dashboard link]"
- Rollback notice: "Initiating rollback for <shortname> at 11:03 UTC due to QA metric regression > threshold. Traffic reverted to previous model/version. Postmortem TBD."

Rollback heuristics (simple, conservative):
- Auto-rollback: if any critical probe crosses hard threshold (examples: error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, p99 latency > 2x baseline, QA delta worse than -2 points) within two consecutive sweeps -> auto-rollback and page oncall
- Soft rollback (manual): multiple small degradations across non-critical metrics -> pause and escalate to owner + oncall for decision

Edgecases and deconflicts:
- Parallel microreleases: avoid overlapping exposures for edits that touch the same service or prompt family. If unavoidable, serialize by timebox windows.
- Experiment interference: flag active A/B experiments in the release note; if overlap detected, default to not progressing beyond 2% until owners coordinate
- Low traffic slices: if slice doesn't reach minimum sample size for QA probes, hold progression until sample thresholds are met or use synthetic probe traffic

Operational runbook snippets (to paste into console):
- Start: POST /rollouts with {"shortname": "xxx", "traffic": [0.5, 2, 5], "sweeps": 10m} -> returns rollout_id
- Advance: POST /rollouts/<id>/advance -> triggers sweep and increments slice if pass
- Pause: POST /rollouts/<id>/pause -> hold progression, alert owner
- Rollback: POST /rollouts/<id>/rollback -> revert to previous stable version and notify oncall

Open questions / TODOs:
- Determine quantitative thresholds for 'QA metric' across our major prompt families (action: Priya to run historical comparison on 6 prompt families by Feb 7)
- Integrate sweep summaries into Console's rollout timeline UI (engineering effort estimate needed)
- Templateize the small curated prompt sets per product area (owner: Diego)
- Add a lightweight synthetic load generator for low-traffic slices to reach sample sizes without exposing production users

Notes to self (work-in-progress style):
- Keep microreleases conservative; they are meant to de-risk, not speed past safety
- Consider a "microrelease label" on the dashboard so support and CS can immediately see a change was small and recent
- Think about adding an "opt-out" header for partners that explicitly want to ignore microreleases in favor of pinned model versions

References and quick links:
- JIRA: JIRA-RD-987 (microrelease infra backlog)
- Confluence spec: CONFLUENCE-1234 (rollout lifecycle foundation)
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/412

Appendix: minimal sample sweep output format (csv-friendly):
- timestamp, rollout_id, slice_pct, p50_ms, p95_ms, error_rate_pct, qa_delta, probe_count, status
- 2025-02-03T10:15:00Z, r-312, 0.5, 45, 182, 0.03, -0.6, 128, ALERT

End of doc — this is a working draft. Expect changes as we run the first two microreleases and learn.
